abstract: Maintains marine pollution containment records, defueling permits, and spill response statuses
system_message:
You are Maritime environmental officer (ENV). The Maritime environmental officer (ENV) oversees marine pollution containment documentation, defueling authorizations, and spill response readiness assessments. In this capacity, the officer records and verifies offshore barrier deployments, bunker lightering clearances, and emergency counter-pollution inventory logs across salvage proposals.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains marine pollution containment records, defueling permits, and spill response statuses（POLL）
information_points.content:
ENV-POLL-U6F：Under the Direct Flank Towage and Pontoon Lightering Plan, the pollutant containment barrier is deployed around the vessel perimeter and shoreline boundary, and bunker fuel offloading is permitted by the coastal maritime environmental authority.
ENV-POLL-HEO：For the Stern Pull and High-Capacity Nitrogen De-Ballasting Plan, the on-scene audit confirms that continuous pollutant containment barriers along the vessel perimeter and sensitive shoreline boundary are deployed. Additionally, bunker fuel offloading is permitted for lightering heavy fuel oil and diesel service tanks.
ENV-POLL-YDY：For the Rotational Multi-Tug Grounding Scour and Pull Plan, the pollutant containment barrier is not deployed along the vessel perimeter and downstream shoreline boundary, while bunker fuel offloading is permitted for the casualty's service tanks.

information_points.title: Dispersant stockpile logistics（DISP）
information_points.content:
ENV-DISP-0OL：Under the Direct Flank Towage and Pontoon Lightering Plan, the approved bio-dispersant inventory stands at 2000 L in the counter-pollution stockpile.
ENV-DISP-UM3：For the Rotational Multi-Tug Grounding Scour and Pull Plan, the verified approved bio-dispersant inventory available for emergency response is 3500 L.
ENV-DISP-FPY：The Stern Pull and High-Capacity Nitrogen De-Ballasting Plan has an approved bio-dispersant inventory of 5000 L pre-staged in the emergency counter-pollution store.
